obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N71-R04)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data on MID-T or MID-F, including a common point of purchase notice
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise
notify: Acquiring bank merchant risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1 - card brand rule applied through the acquirer, not law
trigger: Discovery of evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that handles it
deadline: Within 3 calendar days
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Visa Level 2 merchant
clock_starts: Discovery of evidence raising a reasonable suspicion

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2
trigger: After notifying Visa
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa; include PCI DSS compliance documentation when available or requested
notify: Visa and the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Security Manager and Chief Financial Officer

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
deadline: Within 3 calendar days; provided through the acquirer or processor
notify: Visa (via the acquirer or the payment partner)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the payment partner can extract card numbers used on affected pages in the window
clock_starts: Whichever of the three events comes first

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator (PFI); Level 1 and Level 2 merchants are among the entities more likely to be required
deadline: Within 5 business days: contract with a PFI and tell Visa the PFI and lead investigator; preliminary report within 5 business days of signing; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation. The PFI must not have served the company as QSA, advisor, consultant, or monitoring provider in the past 3 years
notify: Visa and the acquirer (the PFI reports directly to Visa)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Visa requires it
owner: Chief Financial Officer and General Counsel

citation: Mastercard, American Express, and Discover operating rules - applied through the acquirer, not law
trigger: Suspected compromise of those brands' card data
deadline: Per acquirer and brand instructions (not verified here)
notify: Acquirer; card brands through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; these rules were not verified

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a card number and any required security code (501.171(1)(g)1.a.(III)), and an email address with a password (501.171(1)(g)1.b.). A patron export of names, emails, phones, addresses, and order history alone is not personal information under this definition
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a)); substitute notice allowed if direct notice would cost more than $250,000 or reach more than 500,000 people
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for skimmed card data with security codes
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe one occurred

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination, keep it at least 5 years, and give it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (the 15-day extension applies only to the notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000
clock_starts: When circumstances requiring the notices are discovered

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: The ticketing vendor, payment partner, or another agent has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: No later than 10 days following the agent's determination of the breach; the company then gives the notices above
notify: The company (General Counsel and Security Manager)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - also add a 72-hour Tier 1 contract term (STD-03; POAM-021)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 29% of ticket buyers live outside Florida; some states' definitions may cover the patron export even where Florida's does not

trigger: Security incident affecting County PAC data or services
deadline: Within 48 hours
notify: County contract administrator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes from 2027-07-01

trigger: Suspected security incident or event-day outage with financial loss
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging incident vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

citation: n/a (voluntary); Visa WTDIC recommends the U.S. Secret Service for card compromises
trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card data, account takeover, or extortion
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0 to 2)
notify: U.S. Secret Service field office; FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment (for example a demand not to publish the patron export)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a demand is made. Applies to all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). If finalized as proposed, entities in a critical infrastructure sector that exceed their SBA size standard would be covered; the company is above its SBA standard and in the Commercial Facilities Sector

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held; not an SEC registrant

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a Nevada gaming licensee
deadline: Notify the Chair within 24 hours of activating the incident response plan; initial report within 5 calendar days; written updates every 30 days
notify: Chair of the Nevada Gaming Control Board
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no gaming license and operates only in Florida (N71-R01)

trigger: Suspicious activity at a casino or card club
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection of facts that may be a basis for filing
notify: FinCEN
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a casino or card club (N71-R03)

trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
